'''Ira Borah Bernstein''' (November 8, 1924 – October 8, 2024) was an American theoretical physicist specializing in [[plasma physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11410020.html|title=Bernstein, Ira B.|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-13}}</ref> He was the first person to formulate the theory of [[Waves in plasmas|electrostatic waves]] propagating in a [[Magnetised Plasma|magnetized plasma]] in 1958, which are now commonly known as Bernstein waves in [[plasma physics]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bernstein|first=Ira B.|date=1958|title=Waves in a Plasma in a Magnetic Field|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.109.10|journal=Physical Review|volume=109|issue=1|pages=10–21|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.109.10|hdl=2027/mdp.39015095022995|hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Bernstein's other theoretical contributions include the development of the energy principle in the study of [[plasma instabilities]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bernstein|first1=I. B.|last2=Frieman|first2=E. A.|last3=Kruskal|first3=Martin David|last4=Kulsrud|first4=R. M.|last5=Chandrasekhar|first5=Subrahmanyan|date=1958|title=An energy principle for hydromagnetic stability problems|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/abs/10.1098/rspa.1958.0023|journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A. Mathematical and Physical Sciences|volume=244|issue=1236|pages=17–40|doi=10.1098/rspa.1958.0023|hdl=2027/mdp.39015095022813|s2cid=13304733 |hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> as well as formulating the exact (one-dimensional) solution to electrostatic wave propagation in an unmagnetized plasma also known as [[Bernstein–Greene–Kruskal modes]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bernstein|first1=Ira B.|last2=Greene|first2=John M.|last3=Kruskal|first3=Martin D.|date=1957|title=Exact Nonlinear Plasma Oscillations|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.108.546|journal=Physical Review|volume=108|issue=3|pages=546–550|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.108.546|hdl=2027/mdp.39015095115203|hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Bernstein studied chemical engineering at the [[City College of New York]] (Baccalaureate 1944)<ref>Biographical data from Lisl Goodman: ''Death and the creative life: conversations with prominent artists and scientists'', Springer 1981 and ''Burning Plasma: bringing a star to earth'', National Research Council</ref> and in 1950 received his PhD from [[New York University]] with his thesis entitled "Improved Calculations on Cascade Shower Theory". From 1950 to 1954, he worked at the [[Westinghouse Electric (1886)|Westinghouse]] research laboratories. From 1954 to 1964, he was a scientist at the [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]], where he was a participant as a senior scientist in Project Matterhorn when the project involved secret U.S. government research on magnetic fusion. In 1964, he became a professor for applied physics at [[Yale University]], where he was from 1994 "Carl A. Morse" Professor for Mechanical Engineering and Applied Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fas.yale.edu/book/faculty-retirement-tributes-2003/ira-b-bernstein|title=Ira B. Bernstein {{!}} Faculty of Arts and Sciences|website=fas.yale.edu|access-date=2020-02-28}}</ref> In 2004, he retired with the rank of [[professor emeritus]].

He was a research consultant with the research laboratories of [[United Technologies]] and [[RCA Corporation|RCA]], the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]], and the [[Naval Research Laboratory]]. He was a member of the Fusion Policy Advisory Committee and the Consulting Committee for Fusion Energy at the U.S. Department of Energy.

Bernstein died on October 8, 2024, at the age of 99.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ira B. Bernstein |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/ira-b-bernstein-wpi6v3/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=26 July 2025}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1982, Bernstein was awarded the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] from the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2008-08-28|title=APS awards Maxwell Prize to Bernstein|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.2915598|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=36|issue=4|pages=70|doi=10.1063/1.2915598|issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1984, he was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/ira-b-bernstein-wpi6v3/|title=Ira Bernstein|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2020-02-28}}</ref>
